land.text: the whole of the absolute monarchy of Siam, which became a constitutional monarchy on 24 June 1932

Cliopatria cuts its Rattanakosin row at 1931 and starts this row in 1932. The colour agent may keep one colour for both rows (rule 2).

region.text: Siam as an absolute monarchy became a constitutional monarchy; Cliopatria's Kingdom of Thailand shape is modern Thailand

ledger.note: 1932: Siam becomes a constitutional monarchy (24 June). The page's infobox gives 'Constitutional monarchy: 24 June 1932'; it names no border. Same state as the Rattanakosin Kingdom, which Cliopatria ends in 1931.

1939: Siam is renamed Thailand (24 June). The page gives 'changed to Thailand' on 24 June 1939 (the Thailand in World War II page puts the nationalist policy at 23 June). The page is silent on the reversion to Siam in 1945 and the final name in 1948-49, so no further rename is recorded.

ledger.note: 1941: the Franco-Thai War ends. A general ceasefire took effect at 10:00 on 28 January, preliminary armistice documents were signed aboard the cruiser Natori on 31 January 1941 and 'On 9 May, a peace treaty was signed in Tokyo' (the page gives no year for the treaty; 1941 by context). The zone stays Thai-held throughout.

ledger.note: 1942: the Thai Phayap Army takes the Shan States. It 'crossed the border into the Shan States on 10 May 1942'; 'Kengtung, the main objective, was captured on 27 May'; 'The Thais remained in control of the Shan States for the remainder of the war'. Cliopatria draws Japan, not Burma, over this land in 1942-1945; the page does not say how or when Japan recognised the Thai hold, so the Thai hold is recorded from the capture. ledger.note: 1943: Japan hands four northern Malay states to Thailand. 'In July 1943, Japanese Prime Minister Hideki Tojo announced that Kedah, Perlis, Kelantan, and Terengganu were to be returned to Thailand'; 'Thailand administered the states as Syburi, Palit, Kalantan and Trangkanu provinces from 18 October 1943' (infobox: 'Four states to Thailand: 18 October 1943'). The land was British Malaya (the British Colonial Empire row) under Japanese occupation.

ledger.note: 1946: Thailand returns the Laotian and Cambodian territory taken in 1941. 'Thailand agreed to cede the territories regained during Japanese presence in the country as the price for admission' to the United Nations; 'all the Thai-occupied territories returned to their pre-war status'; the Anglo-Thai Peace Treaty was signed on 1 January 1946. The page gives no month for the French handover (the Washington Accord is not on the page).

wars.name: Franco-Thai War

zones.text: Laotian territory west of the Mekong (Sayaboury and the Champasak right bank) and the Cambodian provinces of Battambang and Siem Reap that France ceded in 1941; the page's own list of ceded provinces did not load, so the units are the researcher's reading

wars.outcome: Thai victory on the ground; a Japanese-mediated armistice (31 January 1941) and the Tokyo peace treaty (9 May) gave Thailand Laotian and Cambodian provinces; Thailand had to pay six million piastres and accepted only a quarter of the territory it had won. The territory was returned in 1946.

wars.outcome: Thailand, allied to Japan, occupied Kengtung and the Shan States from May 1942, fought the retreating Chinese 93rd Division, and held the Shan States until August 1945.
wars.note: Part of the Burma campaign; Thailand declared war on the United Kingdom and the United States on 25 January 1942. The page names the Chinese 93rd Division; republic-of-china is the Cliopatria row for the Chinese state of the time.

certainty.note: Judgment: a modern surveyed frontier throughout; no page opened gives demarcation dates. The 1941-1946 annexations of Laotian and Cambodian provinces and the 1942-1945 occupation of the Shan States and the Malay states were treaty or occupation lines, drawn as the pages name them but with the extents of the Mekong-side provinces approximate.

notes: Page budget for this state is 1-2 pages; four were opened because the first two were silent on the 1943 and 1945-46 changes. Cliopatria has no shape for the wartime gains: its French Indochina row keeps Sayaboury and Battambang through 1945 and its Thailand row is modern Thailand, so the new keyframes 1941, 1942 and 1944 add them and the ledger returns them in 1945-46. The Franco-Thai War page's list of ceded provinces did not load, so the Laotian and Cambodian units (Xaignabouri, a 60 km radius around Champasak, Batdambang and Siemreab) are the researcher's reading; the Wikipedia article on the war has the province names and a gap-filler should read the 'Aftermath' or the Tokyo convention. The 1946 month and the Washington Accord are not on the pages opened. The page is silent on the renaming to Siam in 1945 and back in 1948/49. No rulers list: the Thailand page names Prajadhipok, Ananda Mahidol (found dead June 1946), Bhumibol (died 2016) and Vajiralongkorn but gives no reign years. Rattanakosin Kingdom (to 1931) and this row are one state; the colour agent should decide whether they share a colour. Counterparts for the wartime events: burma, british-colonial-empire and french-indochina carry the matching loss; Cliopatria draws Japan over the Shan and Malay lands in 1942-45, so empire-of-japan is a neighbour but not the counterpart. The Shan States are drawn as a coordinate radius because the gazetteer has no Kengtung place. [Reviewer se-04-a 2026-10-19: the war 'Cambodian-Thai border clashes of 2025' was removed from wars[] because it lies outside the state's life (1932..2024; validator warning): 'In July 2025, violent clashes broke out between Thailand and Cambodia along their disputed border'; 'On 27 December 2025, both countries mutually agreed to a ceasefire' (Thailand page); no border moved. Wartime Shan States counterpart is british-raj, not burma.]
